title: The Pass by John Donnelly at La Mama #thepass #lamamaetc #heatedrival...
transcript: Making its North American premiere at La Mama, The Pass is a 2014 play that on the surface is a story of queerness in sports, but it's totally different than something like a Heated Rivalry. As is the case for every scene, the opening takes place in a hotel room. Friends and young hopefuls Jason and Ade are on the precipice of their professional soccer careers, and a night of playful and vulgar banter evolves into something more. It actually feels quite stiff, and it wasn't until much later in the play that I realized the extent that both characters had been putting on a performance for one another in that pivotal opening scene. Yet instead of following the thread of their relationship, we end up focusing on Jason's career trajectory in parallel with his psychological unraveling. Having buried himself in his successes and his riches, he's a case study for how personal insecurity, misogyny, and internalized homophobia make a horrible cocktail. Rather than seeking personal clarity, he runs from it and chases dominance instead. Dominance is a major theme here in more than one sense — relating to traditional markers of success, relating to homoerotic relations, and sometimes even relating to sheer power and degradation. It's pretty uncomfortable, but intentionally so. I enjoyed how the piece unfolded as a character study, but the road was bumpy. I felt that it spun its wheels here and there and likely could have accomplished its goal in 30 fewer minutes. But while parts of it are drawn out, contrived, or certainly dated, it still feels sufficiently relevant, even in the Heated Rivalry era. With that, another program for my collection.
classificationReason: First-hand review of The Pass at La Mama; creator shares detailed opinions on the writing, themes, and character work, clearly having seen the production.
